content: Rabeprazole should be stored at room temperature, specifically between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). It can tolerate short-term exposure to temperatures ranging from 59°F to 86°F (15°C to 30°C), such as during transportation. How to Use: Rabeprazole is available as a tablet that should be swallowed whole. Common Side Effects: The most common side effects of rabeprazole include: Pain Sore throat Gas Infection Constipation Headache (in children aged 12 to 17) Diarrhea (in children aged 12 to 17) Nausea and vomiting (in children aged 12 to 17) Stomach pain (in children aged 12 to 17) If any of these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. There may be other side effects not listed here. If you suspect you are experiencing a side effect, contact your healthcare provider or report it to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088 or Health Canada at 1-866-234-2345. Serious Side Effects: While less common, rabeprazole can cause serious side effects. These include: 1. Kidney Problems: Acute tubulointerstitial nephritis, a type of kidney inflammation, can occur at any time during treatment. If you notice a decrease in urine output or blood in your urine, contact your doctor immediately. 2. Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea: Overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut can occur during treatment. Symptoms include watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in stool, severe stomach cramps, and fever. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if these symptoms occur. 3. Severe Skin Reactions: Rabeprazole can cause life-threatening skin conditions such as Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN). Symptoms include painful red or purple skin that peels, flat red rashes or blisters on the skin, mouth, nose, or genitals, and red, painful, watery eyes. Stop taking rabeprazole and seek emergency medical attention if these symptoms develop. 4. DRESS (Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms): This severe allergic reaction can affect multiple organs, including the liver, kidneys, and heart. Symptoms include skin rash, hives, fever, swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, swelling in the legs or feet, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice). Stop taking rabeprazole and seek immediate medical help if these symptoms occur. 5. Lupus: Rabeprazole can trigger or worsen lupus, an autoimmune disorder where the immune system attacks the body. Symptoms include new or worsening joint pain or a rash on the arms or cheeks. Inform your healthcare provider immediately if these symptoms arise. 6. Vitamin B-12 Deficiency: Long-term use of rabeprazole (3 years or more) can reduce vitamin B-12 absorption, leading to deficiency. Symptoms include a sore tongue, weakness, or tingling/numbness in the hands or feet. Stop taking rabeprazole and contact your healthcare provider if these symptoms occur. 7. Hypomagnesemia (Low Magnesium Levels): Rabeprazole can cause dangerously low magnesium levels, which may result in seizures or heart rhythm problems. Those at higher risk include individuals on long-term rabeprazole therapy or those taking other medications that lower magnesium. Symptoms include changes in heart rate, dizziness, muscle spasms, or seizures. Stop taking rabeprazole and contact your healthcare provider if these symptoms occur. 8. Bone Loss and Fractures: Long-term or high-dose use of rabeprazole may increase the risk of bone loss and fractures, particularly in older adults. 9. Severe Allergic Reactions: Rabeprazole can cause serious allergic reactions. Symptoms include breathing difficulties, wheezing, rapid heartbeat, fever, swollen lymph nodes, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty swallowing, itching, rash, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, or fainting. Stop taking rabeprazole and seek emergency medical help if these symptoms occur. Precautions: Allergies: Do not use rabeprazole if you are allergic to rabeprazole, Aciphex, other proton pump inhibitors, or any ingredients in the product. Consult your pharmacist for a full list of ingredients. Drug Interactions: Rabeprazole may interact with certain medications. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: It is unknown if rabeprazole affects pregnancy or passes into breast milk. Inform your healthcare provider if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Usage Instructions: Take rabeprazole as prescribed by your healthcare provider. Do not chew, cut, or crush the tablets. Antacids may be taken alongside rabeprazole if needed. Rabeprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn and may take 1 to 4 days to take full effect. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double doses. Overdose: If you or someone else has taken too much rabeprazole, seek medical help immediately, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222. Uses: Rabeprazole is used to treat conditions caused by excessive stomach acid, including: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) Prevention and treatment of ulcers Erosive esophagitis (EE) Conditions causing excessive stomach acid production Treatment of Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infections Mechanism of Action: Rabeprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Dosage Forms: Rabeprazole is available as 20 mg delayed-release oral tablets under the brand name Aciphex and as generic rabeprazole. Storage: Store rabeprazole at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C). It can tolerate short-term exposure to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C), such as during transportation.
